title: Modeling with Exponential, Logarithmic, Rational and Power Functions
seo_title: Precalculus Modeling with Functions Worksheets (TEKS P.2N)
standard_text: P.2N analyze situations modeled by functions, including exponential, logarithmic, rational, polynomial, and power functions, to solve real-world problems
meta_desc: Free Precalculus modeling worksheets for Texas TEKS P.2N: half-life, continuous growth, pH, decibels and earthquakes, rational and power function models. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Choose the model by how the quantity changes.
key_sub: One step on a log scale means 10 times as much.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Exponential: growth or decay by the same factor each period. Half-life: A = A0(12)t/h. Continuous: A = Pert.
  • Logarithmic scales (pH, decibels, Richter) count powers of 10: one step means 10 times as much.
  • Rational models divide by a changing amount, like average cost or the strength of a mixture.
  • Power models y = kxn: area grows with the square of length, volume with the cube.

Examples

Example

Half-life 5 days, 80 mg, 15 days

15 ÷ 5 = 3 half-lives

80 ÷ 23

Answer: 10 mg

Example

pH with [H+] = 10−4

−log 10−4 = 4

Answer: pH 4

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Dividing by the half-lifet ÷ h is the exponent of 12.
Reading a log scale as linearMagnitude 6 shakes 10 times as much as 5.
Squaring for volumeVolume uses the cube of the scale factor.

faq.a: Analyze situations modeled by functions, including exponential, logarithmic, rational, and polynomial, and power functions, to solve real-world problems.

faq.q: How do you choose a model?
faq.a: Equal factors: exponential. Powers of 10 on a scale: logarithmic. Dividing by a quantity: rational. A fixed power of x: power.

faq.q: Why does continuous growth use e?
faq.a: It is the limit of compounding more and more often.

faq.q: Is a log scale a straight scale?
faq.a: No. Equal steps mean equal ratios.
